packet.title: No step limit in the sxml command (implementation)
packet.summary: Removes the evaluation step limit from the sxml command by setting its step bound to UINT64_MAX, while the library's default stays for embedders and the JavaScript package.

body.p: After (the owner: the sxml command sets no evaluation step limit). Today the command leaves maximum_evaluation_step_count at 0, the library's default of 10^8 steps (, ), about 2 s of work after to ; a long batch job such as a Schematron compile cannot finish, and there is no option to raise it. The library's default stays for embedders and the JavaScript package; the drivers keep their own bounds (, ).

item.p: Mechanism: the command's processor configuration asks for no step bound. If the header has no way to say "no bound" (0 means the default), use the largest value and say so in the decision record, or propose a named constant under "## Proposed" if that reads better (PACKET.md step 4).

Owns: apps/sxml/ (the processor configuration only), the CLI tests that rely on the step limit, docs/CLI.md, and the book's pages that describe the command stopping: performance.md ("The step limit"), appendix-differences.md, ixml-performance.md, javascript.md (which keeps the default, but cites the chapter).

Done when: a command that ran into the bound runs to its end (an example that took more than 10^8 steps); the book's examples match (tools/check-book-examples.sh); the CLI tests pass. Done 2026-10-28 (): the command's processor configuration sets the step bound to UINT64_MAX (0 would mean the default); the CLI test xpath_no_step_limit runs a comparison charged 4 x 10^8 steps to its end; the book's step-limit pages and docs/CLI.md updated.
